He who dreads death dreads either the extinction of all sense or the experience of a new one. If all sense be extinguished, there can be no sense of evil. If a different sort of sense be acquired you become a different creature, and do not cease to live.

output.reason: The passage treats death as a natural transition rather than a welcome escape, and it neither counsels nor licenses ending one's life; it merely reflects on the philosophical possibility of a different existence after death.
